{{Short description|2D supersymmetric generalization to the conformal algebra}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:''N'' = 2 superconformal algebra}}
In [[mathematical physics]], the''' 2D ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 superconformal algebra''' is an infinite-dimensional [[Lie superalgebra]], related to [[supersymmetry]], that occurs in [[string theory]] and [[two-dimensional conformal field theory]]. It has important applications in [[mirror symmetry (string theory)|mirror symmetry]]. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt | last1=Ademollo | first1=M. | last2=Brink | first2=L. | last3=D'Adda | first3=A. | last4=D'Auria | first4=R. | last5=Napolitano | first5=E. | last6=Sciuto | first6=S. | last7=Giudice | first7=E. Del | last8=Vecchia | first8=P. Di | last9=Ferrara | first9=S. | last10=Gliozzi | first10=F. | last11=Musto | first11=R. | last12=Pettorino | first12=R. | title=Supersymmetric strings and colour confinement | doi=10.1016/0370-2693(76)90061-7 | year=1976 | journal=Physics Letters B | volume=62 | issue=1 | pages=105–110}} as a gauge algebra of the U(1) fermionic string.

==Definition==

There are two slightly different ways to describe the ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 superconformal algebra, called the ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 Ramond algebra and the ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 Neveu–Schwarz algebra, which are isomorphic (see below) but differ in the choice of [[standard basis]]. 
The '''''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 superconformal algebra''' is the Lie superalgebra with basis of even elements ''c'', ''L''<sub>''n''</sub>, ''J''<sub>''n''</sub>, for ''n'' an [[integer]], and odd elements ''G''{{su|p=+|b=''r''}}, ''G''{{su|p=&minus;|b=''r''}}, where <math>r\in {\mathbb Z}</math> (for the Ramond basis) or <math display="inline">r\in {1\over 2}+{\mathbb Z}</math> (for the Neveu–Schwarz basis) defined by the following relations:<ref>{{harvnb|Green|Schwarz|Witten|1988a|pp=240–241}}</ref>

::''c'' is in the center
::<math>[L_m,L_n] = \left(m-n\right) L_{m+n} + {c\over 12} \left(m^3-m\right) \delta_{m+n,0}</math>
::<math>[L_m,\,J_n]=-nJ_{m+n}</math>
::<math>[J_m,J_n] = {c\over 3} m\delta_{m+n,0}</math>
::<math>\{G_r^+,G_s^-\} = L_{r+s} + {1\over 2} \left(r-s\right) J_{r+s} + {c\over 6} \left(r^2-{1\over 4}\right) \delta_{r+s,0}</math>
::<math>\{G_r^+,G_s^+\} = 0 = \{G_r^-,G_s^-\}</math>
::<math>[L_m,G_r^{\pm}] = \left( {m\over 2}-r \right) G^\pm_{r+m}</math>
::<math>[J_m,G_r^\pm]= \pm G_{m+r}^\pm</math>

If <math>r,s\in {\mathbb Z}</math> in these relations, this yields the
'''''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 Ramond algebra'''; while if <math display="inline">r,s\in {1\over 2}+{\mathbb Z}</math> are half-integers, it gives the '''''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 Neveu–Schwarz algebra'''. The operators <math>L_n</math> generate a Lie subalgebra isomorphic to the [[Virasoro algebra]]. Together with the operators <math>G_r=G_r^+ + G_r^-</math>, they generate a Lie superalgebra isomorphic to the [[super Virasoro algebra]],
giving the Ramond algebra if <math>r,s</math> are integers and the Neveu–Schwarz algebra otherwise. When represented as operators on a [[inner product space|complex inner product space]], <math>c</math> is taken to act as multiplication by a real scalar, denoted by the same letter and called the ''central charge'', and the adjoint structure is as follows:

:<math>{L_n^*=L_{-n}, \,\, J_m^*=J_{-m}, \,\,(G_r^\pm)^*=G_{-r}^\mp, \,\,c^*=c}</math>

==Properties==
*The ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 Ramond and Neveu–Schwarz algebras are isomorphic by the spectral shift isomorphism <math>\alpha</math> of {{harvtxt|Schwimmer|Seiberg|1987}}: <math display="block">\alpha(L_n)=L_n +{1\over 2} J_n + {c\over 24}\delta_{n,0}</math> <math display="block">\alpha(J_n)=J_n +{c\over 6}\delta_{n,0}</math> <math display="block">\alpha(G_r^\pm)=G_{r\pm {1\over 2}}^\pm</math> with inverse: <math display="block">\alpha^{-1}(L_n)=L_n -{1\over 2} J_n + {c\over 24}\delta_{n,0}</math> <math display="block">\alpha^{-1}(J_n)=J_n -{c\over 6}\delta_{n,0}</math> <math display="block">\alpha^{-1}(G_r^\pm)=G_{r\mp {1\over 2}}^\pm</math>
*In the ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 Ramond algebra, the zero mode operators <math>L_0</math>, <math>J_0</math>, <math>G_0^\pm</math> and the constants form a five-dimensional Lie superalgebra. They satisfy the same relations as the fundamental operators in [[Kähler manifold|Kähler geometry]], with <math>L_0</math> corresponding to the Laplacian, <math>J_0</math> the degree operator, and <math>G_0^\pm</math> the <math>\partial</math> and <math>\overline{\partial}</math> operators.
*Even integer powers of the spectral shift give automorphisms of the ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 superconformal algebras, called spectral shift automorphisms. Another automorphism <math>\beta</math>, of period two, is given by <math display="block">\beta(L_m) = L_m ,</math> <math display="block">\beta(J_m)=-J_m-{c\over 3} \delta_{m,0},</math> <math display="block">\beta(G_r^\pm)=G_r^\mp</math> In terms of Kähler operators, <math>\beta</math> corresponds to conjugating the complex structure. Since <math>\beta\alpha \beta^{-1}=\alpha^{-1}</math>, the automorphisms <math>\alpha^2</math> and <math>\beta</math> generate a group of automorphisms of the ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 superconformal algebra isomorphic to the [[infinite dihedral group]] <math>{\Z}\rtimes {\Z}_2</math>.
*Twisted operators <math display="inline">{\mathcal L}_n=L_n+ {1\over 2} (n+1)J_n</math> were introduced by {{harvtxt|Eguchi|Yang|1990}} and satisfy: <math display="block">[{\mathcal L}_m,{\mathcal L}_n] = (m-n) {\mathcal L}_{m+n}</math> so that these operators satisfy the Virasoro relation with [[central charge]] 0. The constant <math>c</math> still appears in the relations for <math>J_m</math> and the modified relations <math display="block">[{\mathcal L}_m,J_n] = -nJ_{m+n} + {c \over 6} \left(m^2 + m \right) \delta_{m+n,0}</math> <math display="block">\{G_r^+,G_s^-\} = 2{\mathcal L}_{r+s}-2sJ_{r+s} + {c\over 3} \left(m^2+m\right) \delta_{m+n,0}</math>

==Constructions==

===Free field construction===
{{harvs|last1=Green|last2=Schwarz|last3=Witten|year=1988a|year2=1988b|txt}} give a construction using two commuting real [[bosonic field]]s <math>(a_n)</math>, <math>(b_n)</math>

:<math> {[a_m,a_n]={m\over 2}\delta_{m+n,0},\,\,\,\, [b_m,b_n]={m\over 2}\delta_{m+n,0}},
\,\,\,\, a_n^*=a_{-n},\,\,\,\, b_n^*=b_{-n}</math>

and a complex [[fermionic field]] <math>(e_r)</math>

:<math> \{e_r,e^*_s\}=\delta_{r,s},\,\,\,\, \{e_r,e_s\}=0.</math>

<math>L_n</math> is defined to the sum of the Virasoro operators naturally associated with each of the three systems

:<math>L_n = \sum_m : a_{-m+n} a_m  : + \sum_m : b_{-m+n} b_m : + \sum_r \left(r+{n\over 2}\right): e^*_{r}e_{n+r} :</math>

where [[normal ordering]] has been used for bosons and fermions.

The current operator <math> J_n</math> is defined by the standard construction from fermions

:<math>J_n = \sum_r : e_r^*e_{n+r} : </math>

and the two supersymmetric operators <math> G_r^\pm</math> by

:<math> G^+_r=\sum (a_{-m} + i b_{-m}) \cdot e_{r+m},\,\,\,\, G_r^-=\sum (a_{r+m} - ib_{r+m}) \cdot e^*_{m}</math>

This yields an ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 Neveu–Schwarz algebra with&nbsp;''c''&nbsp;=&nbsp;3.

===SU(2) supersymmetric coset construction===
{{harvtxt|Di Vecchia|Petersen|Yu|Zheng|1986}} gave a coset construction of the ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 superconformal algebras, generalizing the [[coset construction]]s of {{harvtxt|Goddard|Kent|Olive|1986}} for the discrete series representations of the Virasoro and super Virasoro algebra. Given a representation of the [[affine Kac–Moody algebra]] of [[SU(2)]] at level <math>\ell</math> with basis <math>E_n,F_n,H_n</math> satisfying
:<math>[H_m,H_n]=2m\ell\delta_{n+m,0},</math>
:<math>[E_m,F_n]=H_{m+n}+m \ell\delta_{m+n,0},</math>
:<math>[H_m,E_n]=2E_{m+n},</math>
:<math>[H_m,F_n]=-2F_{m+n},</math>
the supersymmetric generators are defined by
:<math> G^+_r = (\ell/2+ 1)^{-1/2} \sum E_{-m} \cdot e_{m+r}, \,\,\, G^-_r = (\ell/2 +1 )^{-1/2} \sum F_{r+m}\cdot e_m^*.</math>
This yields the N=2 superconformal algebra with 
:<math>c=3\ell/(\ell+2) .</math>
The algebra commutes with the bosonic operators 
:<math>X_n=H_n - 2 \sum_r : e_r^*e_{n+r} :.</math>
The space of [[physical state]]s consists of [[eigenvector]]s of <math>X_0</math> simultaneously annihilated  by the <math>X_n</math>'s for positive <math>n</math> and the supercharge operator 
:<math>Q=G_{1/2}^+ + G_{-1/2}^-</math> (Neveu–Schwarz)
:<math>Q=G_0^+ +G_0^-.</math> (Ramond)
The supercharge operator commutes with the action of the affine Weyl group and the physical states lie in a single orbit of this group, a fact which implies the [[Weyl-Kac character formula]].<ref name=Wassermann2010>{{harvnb|Wassermann|2010}}</ref>

===Kazama–Suzuki supersymmetric coset construction===
{{harvtxt|Kazama|Suzuki|1989}} generalized the SU(2) coset construction to any pair consisting of a simple [[compact Lie group]] <math>G</math> and a closed subgroup <math>H</math> of maximal rank, i.e. containing a [[maximal torus]] <math>T</math> of <math>G</math>, with the additional condition that the dimension of the centre of <math>H</math> is non-zero. In this case the compact [[Hermitian symmetric space]] <math>G/H</math> is a Kähler manifold, for example when <math>H=T</math>. The physical states lie in a single orbit of the affine Weyl group, which again implies the Weyl–Kac character formula for the affine Kac–Moody algebra of <math>G</math>.<ref name=Wassermann2010 />
